findings.claim: The patch removes the fail-fast IllegalStateException("Multiple crypto providers loaded ...") and replaces it with selection by order(). DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. When two of them are on the classpath, the stable sort lets ServiceLoader/classpath order pick the winner silently, and the losers are only logged at DEBUG. A FIPS deployment with a stray keycloak-crypto-default jar can therefore run on the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider instead of failing at startup.
findings.evidence: All three seats cite the ties: DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83-84, WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76-77 and FIPS1402Provider.java:114-115 all return 200. sorted(...) is stable. The pre-patch detectProvider threw. Quarkus is unaffected because KeycloakRecorder.java:214 uses setProvider. Affected init() callers: services KeycloakApplication.java:89, admin-cli Globals.java:44 (its dist packages both the default and fips1402 jars), testsuite CryptoInitRule.java:14 and now AuthzClient.create. mattpocock and superpowers note that the patch has no test of the new selection logic. All seats say this is reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test before fixing, as proposed by superpowers: put two order-200 CryptoProviders on the ServiceLoader path and assert that CryptoIntegration.init throws. It throws on base 10aca55 and returns a provider on HEAD 79d11c4. Smallest fix: keep the throw when the top two providers have equal order(), so ordering only breaks real differences (100 vs 200). Not yet reproduced; the gate was not run.

verifier.reason: CryptoIntegration.java:56-71 now sorts by order() and returns the first provider, where it used to throw on multiple providers; other providers are only logged at debugf (:69). DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200 (patch lines 768-771, 792-795, 808-811), so with two on the classpath the stable sort picks whichever ServiceLoader lists first. The admin-cli example is overstated: ClassLoaderUtil.java:41 builds a classloader with only the FIPS or only the default jars, but non-Quarkus init() callers such as KeycloakApplication are exposed.

findings.claim: int order() is added as an abstract method, with no default, to the public SPI interface CryptoProvider in keycloak-common. External implementations stop compiling. An implementation already compiled against the old interface and loaded through ServiceLoader throws AbstractMethodError when detectProvider's comparator calls order(), which crashes CryptoIntegration.init. The patch has no release note or upgrade-guide entry.
findings.evidence: superpowers rated it Important: keycloak-common is consumed outside this repo, e.g. by the separate keycloak-client authz-client that this commit mirrors. open-code-review rated it Minor: AbstractMethodError from Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order) once two or more providers are found, all in-repo implementations are covered (Fips1402StrictCryptoProvider by inheritance), and there is no migration note. mattpocock rated it Minor: PR-CHECKLIST.md requires release notes and upgrade guide where applicable, CONTRIBUTING.md #8 requires documentation, and grep -rl CryptoProvider docs finds nothing. ponytail raised the same AbstractMethodError claim as a side note to its duplication finding. Severity is normalised up to Important because the failure is a runtime crash of the init path for any external provider. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test before fixing: load, via ServiceLoader, a CryptoProvider class compiled against the pre-patch interface (no order()) next to a second provider, and assert that init succeeds. It fails with AbstractMethodError on HEAD. Smallest fix: give order() a default in the interface. Add an upgrade note if the method stays abstract. If no red can be built inside the repo, defer as unverified with this exact check. Severity split between seats: Important (superpowers) vs Minor (open-code-review, mattpocock, ponytail).

verifier.reason: The patch adds `int order();` with no default at CryptoProvider.java:44, and the new `.sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed())` in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider (change.patch:713) calls it. External implementations therefore stop compiling, an old compiled one throws AbstractMethodError once two or more providers are found, and the patch adds no docs or upgrade note. One caveat: a lone old provider never reaches the comparator, and two providers already failed before this patch with IllegalStateException (patch:718-720), so the runtime crash is not new; the compile break and missing upgrade note are.

verifier.reason: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114-115, each call builds a new ASN1Encoder and the result is never used. write() only fills that encoder's own private ByteArrayOutputStream (ASN1Encoder per the patch, lines 293-306), so nothing else changes. The returned value is rebuilt from scratch at lines 117-121.

findings.claim: The test uses one default KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") key (P-256, or P-384 on some JDKs) for ES256, ES384 and ES512, and only asserts a self round-trip. So the P-521-sized signatures, the DER long-form length paths (ASN1Encoder.writeLength and ASN1Decoder.readLength when length > 127) and independent correctness of the encoding are never exercised. An encoder/decoder bug that is symmetric would pass.
findings.evidence: mattpocock #3 (lines 42, 65-71; cites CONTRIBUTING.md #7 and PR-CHECKLIST.md 'sufficient test coverage'), open-code-review #6 (lines 42, 56; the asn1Des output is never checked with Signature.verify), superpowers #4 (ES512 with a P-256 key gives about 70 bytes of DER). superpowers' standalone javac harness ran 500 signatures each on P-256, P-384 and P-521 against SHAxxxwithECDSAinP1363Format with 0 failures, including the long-form path. So this is a test gap, not a codec bug.
findings.reason: Accepted as a test gap. Generate a key per curve (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1) and check the output independently with SHAxxxwithECDSAinP1363Format or Signature.verify. Minor; no red is expected because superpowers' harness shows the codec is correct.

verifier.reason: ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 creates a single default `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` key (P-256, or P-384 on newer JDKs) and uses it for ES256, ES384 and ES512. Lines 53-56 only check that the codec's own decode/encode/decode output matches itself, and never check the result with `Signature.verify` or a P1363 reference. With those keys the DER signature stays under 128 bytes, so the long-form length branches (ASN1Encoder.java:67 and ASN1Decoder.java:137) are never run, and a bug that is the same in both directions would pass.

findings.claim: AuthzClient.create now sets JVM-global crypto state, and the first caller wins. If only AuthzClientCryptoProvider is visible, it is locked in as the provider. It throws UnsupportedOperationException for most methods, and its getBouncyCastleProvider() (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61-66) fixes BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER to the JDK keystore provider (usually SUN). A later KeycloakApplication init in the same JVM then does nothing.

Reasoned.

findings.claim: The DER parsing is lenient. Tag checks compare only tag & 0x1f, ignoring the class and constructed bits. readInteger with length 0 throws NumberFormatException rather than IOException. Trailing bytes after the sequence are ignored.
findings.evidence: open-code-review #5 (lines 52, 68, 73). It notes the input is trusted JCA Signature.sign() output on the signer path only, the verifier path only encodes, and ECDSASignatureVerifierContext.verify catches Exception. superpowers reproduced NumberFormatException on '30 04 02 00 02 00' but classed it as behaviour matching intent, so it is not counted as raising this.
findings.reason: Appendix: single seat; not reported and not fixed.

findings.claim: The decoder supports high-tag-number tags and indefinite-length encoding (lines 93-124, 133-135), which its only caller never needs: JDK Signature.sign() DER, always 0x30 with two 0x02 integers and never indefinite length. The indefinite-length branch returns -1, and readInteger would then hit new byte[-1] and throw NegativeArraySizeException, adding a crash path.
findings.evidence: ponytail #4. The only production caller is ECDSASignatureSignerContext (core/.../ECDSASignatureSignerContext.java:33). The crash path is reasoned, not run. Suggested trim is about -25 lines.
